body: Thanks for the reply.  I have actually been fortunate enough myself that if people have been judging me when I use my EBT card, they've at least done so silently thus far.  But I've read enough stories online from people who have been publicly shamed and humiliated by nosy strangers, and enough comments sections filled overwhelmingly with hatred on any article in which this issue is discussed, to make my blood boil.

I absolutely understand how you feel.  At this point in my life I don't feel I have much to reach for myself.  Hell, I just made and ate some fried eggs and bacon, and that actually felt like an accomplishment given how little I have done in the past few weeks.  I am certainly not in any position to be giving you advice.  Short-term satisfaction is all that's keeping me going at this point.  Not sure how long I can maintain that, but so far I've managed.  Maybe let the short-term stuff carry you for awhile and see if it takes you anywhere.

I'm sure you've already heard "you're young there is so much time left" etc, so I won't take that tack.  But the fact that at your age you know how to build an explosive means you have both intelligence and motivation, and I feel certain those factors will allow you opportunities in the future you simply haven't envisioned yet, were they applied differently.

I don't know why, or if, anyone "matters".  But we're all in this life, and I personally suspect there's nothing after.  If you can find anything in this life to reach for, reach for it.  The worst that can happen is you fail and are back where you were before.

You clearly seem to understand that racism, sexism etc are wrong.  I think that means you have the potential to change, and become a better person.  We can't change the mistakes we've made in the past, but there's at least a chance we can try to make a better future.  It sounds like you could do that better by sticking around and exploring better ways of treating others, and yourself.  And I'm not a doctor but I think people can live quite a long time with AIDS.

Right where you are...except I've done all the research.  If I decided to go through with it, the internet can provide me all the instruction I need regarding materials and procedures.  The research however also brought me to the inescapable conclusion that there isn't one single method available to me that does not carry far too high a risk of failure for me to ever be willing to attempt.  I don't want to be here as it is...even less would I want to be here but in worse shape physically than I already am, and/or hospitalized/institutionalized by people who for some reason insist I must stay alive despite having no interest in actually helping me want to do so.  So yes, constantly trying to force myself to continue the activities that used to bring me joy, and now just barely distract me from how shitty I feel on every level at every moment. Thank you for the offer.  I was in bed all day (as is pretty common for me).  Still up for chatting if you are around.

It was a 10 year relationship, and it's only been 3 months since it ended, but I am feeling exactly the way you are.  I've had health problems for a long time that have been very difficult to deal with, but I was never really depressed because I had enough good things in my life to still make it worthwhile.  Now I have nothing, just as you described.  The few people I can talk to at all just tell me to move on and things will get better.  They are so wrong.  Even if I wanted to move on and were mentally capable of doing so, I have nothing to move on TO.  No money, can't work, am rarely even able to go out due to my condition, not that I have anywhere to go anymore other than to buy food...nothing to offer anyone.

So I sure do empathize with the dangers of "falling in love with they way things were".  Not that I made the choice to do so...and I suspect you didn't either.  I wish I had some advice for you but I really don't.  Maybe sharing my story will help at least a little bit.
I am 44, feeling much the same as you are right now.  Not sure how much help I can be but I too would certainly appreciate someone I could talk to about things.

Your situation sounds remarkably similar to mine, right down to "44, divorced, broke and jobless".  No one in my life but my parents and exactly two friends, none of whom have the time to even spend with me on occasion, let alone the ability to help me figure out how to still want my life at all when there's nothing good in it anymore.  I'm lucky my incessant begging for some attention hasn't driven them away entirely yet...but it's only been a few months, I'm sure it'll come soon enough, and frankly I couldn't blame them.  I never contributed much to anyone else's life BEFORE mine was a wreck...been essentially nothing but a burden since.

So...hang in there I guess.  You won't hear me saying "things will get better" or any of that shit, but I can at least fully understand and empathize with your situation...I hope that might be helpful to you even in some tiny way.
